design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (shopper_batch_pay_and_tips, category batch).

[1] Why this is a good test. Omar Rashidi (Full-Service Shopper Silver) only asks for the miles he drove on yesterday's Double Delivery Batch (Stop & Shop, Malden Centre) to be paid: 12.4 driven vs a 7.6-mile estimate, mileage pay 3.30. The desk must read the dispute policy, see that the claim is fixed only once the batch carries the not-delivered reversal owed for the wrong-address violation recorded against it (a fact the shopper mentions only if asked why the drive ran long), book that reversal at its own multi-factor amount, hand the shopper the mileage dispute with the claim worked out on the corrected ledger, and approve the adjustment. The test forces reading two prerequisite sentences, reconciling the batch ledger with the shopper's violation and rating ledger and the payout ledger (fees), and 13 factors of arithmetic; no information is missing and each problem has exactly one tool.

[2] Scope snapshot. Occupied by task 0: batch_ext_long_distance_bonus, batch_ext_duplicate_recovery, batch_ext_shown_pay_claim, batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment; tools post_pay_component_6b97a1a8, reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45, submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2, book_pay_adjustment_e97659e1. Claimed here: batch_ext_undelivered_recovery, batch_ext_mileage_claim, batch_ext_mileage_adjustment with reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c, submit_mileage_claim_29030431 (owner user), book_mileage_adjustment_6fe9f3bb. Remaining headroom: none required (M = 2); every extended policy is claimed exactly once. The task-1 flow was first planned on a canceled batch; that plan was dropped before any asset was written because both base time gates (clawback window, dispute window) anchor on batches.completed_date, which a canceled batch never carries.

[3] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --task 1): {"task": 1, "key": "env_0027_grocery_delivery_platform/shopper_batch_pay_and_tips/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]}. Assignment: batch_ext_undelivered_recovery 4, batch_ext_mileage_claim 4, batch_ext_mileage_adjustment 5.

[4] Problem-tree card (chain). Root = batch_ext_mileage_adjustment (the shopper's surface request: pay the miles driven).
 (a) mileage_adjustment -> mileage_claim, kind value_input, gate ma_claim, form state, sentence: "A mileage adjustment is not booked until the batch carries a submitted mileage dispute from the shopper stating a claimed amount." (negated direction; contrapositive of "booked only after the batch carries ..."). False at opening: initial_state holds no batch_pay_disputes row. Resolved by submit_mileage_claim_29030431 (owner user). Skipping it: the adjustment computes 0 instead of 4.03 and the dispute row is absent.
 (b) mileage_claim -> undelivered_recovery, kind value_input, gate mc_standing, form state, sentence: "The mileage claim is not fixed until the batch's earnings entries carry a reversal on the verified not-delivered ground for the orders that wrong-address violations recorded against the batch show as not delivered." False at opening: shopper_events carries a wrong_address violation (3 points, 2026-05-11) against the batch, while the batch's five entries are all batch_pay_posted (no reversal). Resolved by reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c. Skipping it: the claim computes 1.63 instead of 2.35 (mileage standing 3.30 instead of 2.58).
 Four-point test: explicit connective "not ... until" in both; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a submitted mileage dispute on the batch; a not-delivered reversal entry on the batch) naming no action, performer or tool; no code token; hard requirement, scope exactly the condition. Exactly one write brings each state about: only the shopper's mileage filing creates a mileage_underpaid dispute (the shown-pay filing of the charter always files shown_pay_shortfall); only the undelivered recovery writes a reversal on the not-delivered ground (the duplicate recovery writes duplicate_pay). Derivation: sentence + records (wrong_address violation on the batch, no reversal; no dispute) + the depended-on rules' opening sentences ("the pay the batch received for delivering it is taken back by the desk with one reversal against the batch's mileage posting"; "files a mileage dispute on that batch herself") -> one resolving action per edge. The charter carries both directions (task 0 affirmative "only after" twice and negated once; task 1 negated twice), each chosen as the desk would state that wait.
 Topological order: undelivered_recovery -> mileage_claim -> mileage_adjustment (a chain: no parallel prerequisites, so no order freedom). user_scenario names no prerequisite: the wrong-address order surfaces only as an answer to "why did the drive run so long", and the reversal, dispute and filing are reacted to only after the agent raises them. Tools block nothing (task_tools.py bodies: one create plus updates, no condition, no error).

[5] Factor card (handling-time world). Revision round 2 rebuilt UR and MC (audit F2, F3, F4, T1-3, T1-4); every figure below comes from the round-2 run and was checked in exact decimal half-up arithmetic (no half-cent tie in any gold, sensitivity or fall-back figure).
 batch_ext_undelivered_recovery = 0.72 (step 10, opening world). Base amount (plumbing, the baseline paragraph): the not-delivered share of the one mileage posting, 3.30 x 1 wrong-address violation / 2 orders = 1.65.
  - ur_standing_share (parameter, cross shopper): 3 active points -> 0.80; baseline 1.00 -> 0.97.
  - ur_loyalty_allowance (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): Silver (level_min_batches_30d 40) AND MONTHS(2024-01-20, 2026-05-12) = 27 -> 0.20; baseline 0 -> 0.87.
  - ur_verification_timing (parameter, cross shopper): the latest wrong-address violation is dated 2026-05-11 = completion date, 0 days -> 0.15; baseline 0 -> 0.84.
  - ur_settlement_method (method, cross payout, multi-source): instant cashout of 14.00 on 2026-05-11 (less than a month before) AND the Instant Cashout plan charges an instant-cashout fee (0.50) -> amount x 0.75 rounded down; tier 2 (a fee-free plan) would halve and round up; baseline taken in full -> 0.97.
  1.65 x 0.80 - 0.20 - 0.15 = 0.97; x 0.75 = 0.7275 -> 0.72. All at baseline 1.65. Near-miss: the 2-star rating dated 2026-05-12 is the latest shopper event against the batch but not a wrong-address violation (taking its date gives the 1-day tier, 0.10); the expired batch_dropped violation (see MC) would push a ledger-summing reader to five points and the 1.00 standing share.
 batch_ext_mileage_claim = 2.35 (step 12, after the reversal 0.72).
  - mc_claim_tolerance (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): Silver AND 27 months -> 10 percent; baseline type 15 percent -> 2.24.
  - mc_detour_exclusion (method, cross shopper): one wrong_address violation against the batch -> miles beyond the tolerance 12.4 - 7.6 x 1.10 = 4.04, times delivered orders 1 / 2 = 2.02, rounded down to the tenth 2.0; tier 2 (no wrong-address but a late delivery) would halve and round down to a whole mile; baseline all 4.04 -> 3.47.
  - mc_claim_rate (parameter, cross shopper): 3 active points -> type rate 0.50 + 0.05 = 0.55; baseline type rate 0.50 -> 1.92.
  - mc_rated_supplement (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): a 5-star and a 2-star rating -> 0.20; baseline 0 -> 2.15.
  Paid route 7.6 + 2.0 - 1.0 = 8.6; 8.6 x 0.55 + 0.20 - (3.30 - 0.72) = 2.35. All at baseline: (7.6 + 3.66 - 1.0) x 0.50 - 2.58 = 2.55. Near-miss (T1-3): the shopper ledger also holds a batch_dropped violation of 2 points (2026-01-20, on an older dropped batch) and its expiry clearing (2026-04-20, removal_reason expired); a reader who sums every recorded violation reaches 5 points and the "four or more" tier (type rate 0.50, claim 1.92), while the rule reads active points, which the account balance (3) and the clearing row both show.
 batch_ext_mileage_adjustment = 4.03 (step 14).
  - ma_approval_share (parameter, cross shopper): 3 active points -> 0.95; baseline 1.00 -> 4.16.
  - ma_cashout_fee_credit (parameter, cross payout): one instant cashout fee 0.50 on 2026-05-11 -> 0.50; baseline 0 -> 3.51.
  - ma_prompt_credit (parameter, date): dispute 2026-05-12, one day after completion -> 0.40; baseline 0 -> 3.62.
  - ma_long_route_credit (parameter, history, multi-source): posted mileage 3.30 >= 3.00 AND 12.4 >= 1.5 x 7.6 = 11.4 -> 0.75; baseline 0 -> 3.25.
  - ma_tenure_method (method, cross shopper, multi-source): Silver AND 27 months -> sum x 1.04 rounded down; baseline sum as is -> 3.88.
  2.35 x 0.95 + 0.50 + 0.40 + 0.75 = 3.8825; x 1.04 = 4.0378 -> rounded down 4.03. All at baseline 2.35. Near-miss: the 14.00 instant cashout is not a fee; the expired violation again separates active from recorded points.
 Overrides declared: the base mileage_underpaid sentence (in both the claim and, since round 2, the adjustment, audit O3) and the base owed-amount sentence (adjustment).

[6] Base-invariant card.
 Step 10 (batch_pay_reversed): batch_evt_clawback.clawback_window — completed 2026-05-11 day 0, last day 2026-06-10 inclusive, frozen 2026-05-12 day 1; boundary 2026-06-10 allowed, 2026-06-11 not. reverse_once — no reversal names the mileage entry. Ground order_not_delivered_verified is in the Double Delivery Batch clawback_reasons; the verification is the wrong_address violation recorded against the batch (a system record).
 Step 12 (mileage filing, subject batch_completed): policy_scope of batch_evt_pay_calculation and batch_evt_lifecycle.
 Step 14 (batch_pay_adjusted): within_agent_limits — no adjustment for this shopper in the 30 days to 2026-05-12 (0 < 3) and 4.03 <= Double cap 20.00; dispute_window — completed 2026-05-11 day 0, last day 2026-05-18 inclusive, filed 2026-05-12; boundary 2026-05-18 accepted, 2026-05-19 not; one_per_reason — no mileage_underpaid adjustment on the batch. The batch completed on 2026-05-11 and, by the Double type's 24-hour clause, was finalized on 2026-05-12 (status finalized, finalized_date 2026-05-12 in the seed); finalization closes tip changes only, and neither the clawback nor the dispute rules gate on it.

[7] Business-object card. Target: batch B1 (Double Delivery Batch, Stop & Shop, Malden Centre, accepted 2026-05-11T09:12:00). The reversal is booked against the single mileage entry (3.30); the mileage standing counts that entry less reversals on the not-delivered ground; the dispute and the adjustment carry batch_id B1 and the adjustment carries the dispute's reference. The wrong_address violation, both ratings and the payout credits all point at B1; the instant cashout (14.00) and its fee (0.50, source_event_id = the cashout) are the only debits. The shopper's only other batch is a Single Delivery Batch at Market Basket, Everett, dropped by shopper choice on 2026-01-20 before shopping started: it earned nothing (drop forfeits pay), carries no earnings entry, and is excluded from every aggregate here, which reads the target batch only; its batch_dropped violation expired and was cleared on 2026-04-20.

[8] Why each seed row exists. customers (phone, ZIP, email); shopper_accounts (Silver, activated 2024-01-20, 3 active points: loyalty allowance, standing share, tolerance, rate, approval share, tenure method); shopper_events (wrong_address violation on B1: the not-delivered finding, count of shares, timing allowance, detour exclusion; ratings 5 and 2 on B1: rated-service supplement; the batch_dropped violation of 2026-01-20 and its expiry clearing of 2026-04-20: the near-miss between recorded and active points); payout_accounts (Instant Cashout plan, which charges a 0.50 instant-cashout fee: settlement method); payout_events (five credits mirroring the pay entries, the 14.00 cashout and its 0.50 fee: settlement method and cashout-fee credit); batches (B1: miles, orders, dates; the old dropped batch: parent of the expired violation); batch_events (five pay entries on B1; the mileage entry is the reversal's source). Automatic clauses: the 24-hour finalization has run on B1 (finalized 2026-05-12); the dropped batch's violation expired after 90 days and is cleared; the quality bonus 0.50 for the one five-star rating stands; no clause fires on frozen_time. earnings_usd 15.80 equals the ledger; available_balance_usd 1.30 = 15.80 - 14.00 - 0.50; violation_points_balance 3 = 3 + 2 - 2. No cache trap.

[9] Persona design. A calm, tired Silver shopper who knows three figures shown in his app (12.4 driven, 7.6 estimated, 3.30 mileage — all in initial_state), gives phone then ZIP (email as a spare), describes the batch in words, admits the wrong-house delivery only when asked why the drive ran long, has no claimed figure of his own, reacts to the reversal only after the agent raises it, files the mileage dispute with the amount given, and closes on the adjustment. No other ask.

[10] Where a careless agent goes wrong. (i) Filing the claim on the opening ledger (1.63) — the claim's prerequisite sentence waits on the not-delivered reversal. (ii) Missing the reversal because the shopper never asks for it: the wrong_address violation against the batch is in the shopper-event lookup. (iii) Reversing the whole 3.30 entry, or the bare share 1.65 (baseline), instead of applying the standing share, the two allowances and the fee-plan settlement (x 0.75 rounded down). (iv) Using the base mileage_underpaid formula, the type tolerance 15 percent, or all 4.04 miles beyond the tolerance. (v) Summing every recorded violation (5 points, the expired batch_dropped one included) instead of reading the 3 active points — wrong tier in three ladders. (vi) Treating the 2-star rating's date as the verification date, or ignoring it in the supplement. (vii) Rounding the tenure method half up (4.04) instead of down (4.03). (viii) Booking the adjustment before the shopper files.

[11] Standard solution. Locate by phone 6175547709 -> verify with phone + ZIP 02148 -> read shopper account, batches, earnings entries, disputes (none), shopper events, payout account, payout events. Write: reverse 0.72 against the mileage entry on the not-delivered ground (reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c) -> unlock submit_mileage_claim_29030431 and hand it over; the shopper files 2.35 and reads back the dispute reference -> book_mileage_adjustment_6fe9f3bb credits 4.03 against it (mileage_underpaid, shopper account S1) and marks it approved. Terminal batch earnings 15.80 - 0.72 + 4.03 = 19.11.

[12] Verification (executed, revision round 2; scratch evaluator reusing check_compute and the real tools, every figure re-evaluated with exact decimal half-up rounding). Output:
 batch_ext_undelivered_recovery 0.72 (exact 0.72) {ur_standing_share: 0.97, ur_loyalty_allowance: 0.87, ur_verification_timing: 0.84, ur_settlement_method: 0.97, all: 1.65}
 batch_ext_mileage_claim 2.35 (exact 2.35) {mc_claim_tolerance: 2.24, mc_detour_exclusion: 3.47, mc_claim_rate: 1.92, mc_rated_supplement: 2.15, all: 2.55}
 batch_ext_mileage_adjustment 4.03 (exact 4.03) {ma_approval_share: 4.16, ma_cashout_fee_credit: 3.51, ma_prompt_credit: 3.62, ma_long_route_credit: 3.25, ma_tenure_method: 3.88, all: 2.35}
 no tie between float and exact decimal on any figure; claim skip UR 1.63 | adjustment skip MC 0 | terminal earnings 19.11.
 Revision log: round 1 — driven miles 12.0 -> 12.2 to avoid a half-cent claim; status finalized by the 24-hour clause. Round 2 (audit) — UR rebuilt (F2), MC detour and rate ladders rebuilt (F3, F4), near-miss rows seeded (T1-3), batch moved to estimated 7.6 / driven 12.4 miles with a 3.30 mileage posting because every 0.50-rate fall-back over a route ending in an odd hundredth sat on a half cent (T1-4: the round-1 fall-back 3.385 was recorded as 3.38); all computations, tracing and closure texts regenerated.

[13] Closure. undelivered_recovery -> reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c -> 10/amount_usd -> reversal 0.72; mileage_claim -> submit_mileage_claim_29030431 -> 12/claimed_amount_usd -> dispute submitted 2.35; mileage_adjustment -> book_mileage_adjustment_6fe9f3bb -> 14/amount_usd -> adjustment 4.03 and dispute approved. charter_scope = required_documents = computations = the tree; nothing remains open. No handoff.

[14] Masked recomputation from visible context. From the published rules, tool schemas, share-tool returns and persona lines only: the adjustment waits on a submitted mileage dispute; the claim waits on the not-delivered reversal; the reversal is owed because the shopper-event lookup shows a wrong_address violation on the batch. Every input (Silver, activated 2024-01-20, 3 active points with the expired 2-point violation cleared, violation and ratings dated 2026-05-11/12, mileage entry 3.30, 7.6/12.4 miles, 2 orders, Instant Cashout plan with a 0.50 fee and a 14.00 cashout on 2026-05-11, completion 2026-05-11) is returned by a lookup, and 0.72, 2.35, 4.03 follow in that order with no second reading.

[15] Per-task gates are re-run after revision round 2 (results in the difficulty worklog). Manual values gates: the owner=user filing is the shopper's own claim (base "A shopper disputes pay on one batch by submitting a dispute"); every volunteered fact (12.4, 7.6, 3.30, yesterday's batch) is in initial_state; the wrong-house order is disclosed only on question; windows anchor on completed_date (day 0, inclusive); no real-world wait. Every factor of UR and MC is a ladder of three distinct outcomes over conditions that do not restate the policy's scope, and each computation has a near-miss (UR: the 2-star rating's date and the expired violation; MC: the expired violation; MA: the cashout versus its fee).
user_scenario: You are Omar Rashidi, a Cartwise shopper based in Malden who has been doing deliveries for a couple of years. You are calling in the early afternoon, calm but a bit tired of being underpaid on mileage. Your complaint is about the two-order batch you did yesterday morning out of Stop & Shop, Malden Centre: the app shows you drove 12.4 miles on it, the offer's route said 7.6 miles, and the mileage pay on the batch is only $3.30; you want the miles you actually drove paid properly. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 6175547709; when asked to confirm who you are, you give your home ZIP code, 02148, and if one more detail is needed your email, omar.rashidi@postloft.com. You do not know any batch or account number; asked which batch, you say it was yesterday morning, Stop & Shop, Malden Centre, two orders, and it is the only batch you did yesterday. Only if the agent asks why the drive ran so long do you admit that one of the two orders went to the wrong house, the app flagged it afterwards and that customer never got the bags, and you drove around the neighborhood a while sorting it out. If asked what amount you think you are owed, you say you have no idea how the miles are paid and want whatever the rules say. You are fine with the agent fixing things on your batch for you. If the agent tells you some pay has to be taken back because of the order that went to the wrong house, you sigh and say that is fair enough since that customer never got the order. If the agent explains that you have to file the mileage dispute yourself and hands it to you, you file it on that batch with exactly the amount the agent gives you and read back the reference number you get. You do not raise anything else. When the agent tells you the mileage adjustment has been credited, you thank them and hang up.

gold_actions.business_effect: Books a reversal of 0.72 against the batch's mileage entry on the verified not-delivered ground and lowers the batch's earnings.

request_binding.action_semantics: A wrong-address violation recorded against the completed batch verifies one of its two orders was not delivered; the pay received for delivering it is owed back whatever the caller asked, which selects a not-delivered reversal rather than a duplicate-pay reversal or any adjustment.

stage_provenance.fact: The reversal is booked synchronously by this write; the verification it rests on (the violation) is a record present at the opening.

base_preconditions.condition: Posted pay is reversed only on a ground listed in the batch type's clawback_reasons, and only within the clawback window counted from the batch's completion.
A reversal targets one posted or adjusted pay row, named by source_event_id, never more than that row's amount, and each row is reversed at most once.

gold_actions.business_effect: The shopper files his own mileage dispute on the batch claiming 2.35; it stands submitted.

request_binding.action_semantics: The caller says the miles he drove far exceed the route the mileage pay covers; that is the mileage dispute a shopper files himself, not a shown-pay dispute or a component posting.

evidence: user_scenario:the app shows you drove 12.4 miles on it, the offer's route said 7.6 miles, and the mileage pay on the batch is only $3.30
user_scenario:the app shows you drove 12.4 miles on it, the offer's route said 7.6 miles, and the mileage pay on the batch is only $3.30

base_preconditions.condition: Scope: the pay of a completed batch; its eligibility gates concern component postings, none concerns the dispute a shopper files on a completed batch.
Scope: the batch lifecycle through completion and finalization; it has no eligibility gate.

gold_actions.business_effect: Credits the mileage adjustment of 4.03 to the batch against the shopper's dispute and marks the dispute approved.

user_scenario:you want the miles you actually drove paid properly

stage_provenance.fact: The dispute answered was filed by the shopper in this call (step 12).

base_preconditions.condition: The agent may approve an adjustment only while batch_msr_adjustments_30d is below pay_adjustments_per_30d and the adjustment is not above pay_adjustment_agent_cap_usd of the batch's type; otherwise the dispute is escalated (dispute_status escalated) and no adjustment is booked by the agent.
A dispute is accepted only when it is submitted within the dispute window counted from the batch's completion.
Each batch receives at most one adjustment per adjustment_reason.

temporal_feasibility.condition: Posted pay is reversed only on a ground listed in the batch type's clawback_reasons, and only within the clawback window counted from the batch's completion.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The clawback window is counted in calendar days with completed_date as day 0, and the last day to reverse is completed_date plus clawback_window_days, inclusive.

boundary_check.just_before: Completed 2026-05-11 is day 0 and clawback_window_days is 30 for a Double Delivery Batch: 2026-06-10 is the last day; frozen 2026-05-12 (day 1) is inside.
boundary_check.at_boundary: On 2026-06-10 the reversal is still allowed (inclusive); on 2026-06-11 it would be refused.

temporal_feasibility.condition: A dispute is accepted only when it is submitted within the dispute window counted from the batch's completion.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The window is counted in calendar days with completed_date as day 0, and the last day to dispute is completed_date plus pay_dispute_window_days, inclusive.

boundary_check.just_before: Completed 2026-05-11 is day 0 and pay_dispute_window_days is 7: the last day is 2026-05-18; the dispute filed 2026-05-12 (day 1) is inside.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A dispute filed on 2026-05-18 is accepted (inclusive); one filed on 2026-05-19 would not be.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's Cartwise profile by the mobile number he states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the profile's customer reference number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record the in-session identity check with the stated mobile number and home ZIP code.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account detail may be discussed or changed before the caller is confirmed; two matching details are required.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the shopper contractor account: level, first activation date, active violation points.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Level and months since activation decide the not-delivered loyalty allowance, the claim tolerance and the tenure method; active points decide the standing share, the claim rate and the approval share; the account number is carried on the adjustment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the shopper's batches to identify yesterday's Double Delivery Batch at Stop & Shop, Malden Centre: estimated and driven miles, order count, completion date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Estimated 7.6 and driven 12.4 miles drive the qualification, the paid route and the long-route credit; 2 orders drive the not-delivered share and the detour proration; the completion date anchors both windows and the timing and prompt credits. The shopper's older dropped batch is the parent of the expired violation and is excluded from every aggregate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read every earnings entry on the batch.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the single mileage entry of 3.30 (the reversal's source and the mileage standing) and that no reversal stands yet — the claim's prerequisite.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the pay disputes on the batch.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows no mileage dispute exists yet, which the adjustment's prerequisite sentence requires.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the shopper account's violations and ratings.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The wrong_address violation recorded against the batch on 2026-05-11 makes the reversal owed and decides the share count, the timing allowance and the detour exclusion; the five-star and two-star ratings decide the rated-service supplement; the expired batch_dropped violation and its clearing show why only 3 points are active.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the shopper's payout account and plan.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identifies the Instant Cashout plan, which charges an instant-cashout fee (settlement method).
The 14.00 instant cashout on 2026-05-11 selects the settlement method's cash-out tier; its 0.50 fee decides the cashout-fee credit.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for this problem's target tool; no DB effect, unlocked once in the task.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reverse 0.72 of the batch's mileage entry on the verified not-delivered ground.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: batch_ext_undelivered_recovery (state_due) computes amount_usd; the mileage claim is not fixed until this reversal stands.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.batch_id: Value 8d08d992-3f22-47e2-a788-b37238cec82c. Basis: the batch lookup for the verified shopper returns this single batch (Double Delivery Batch, Stop & Shop, Malden Centre, completed 2026-05-11), the one he describes as 'yesterday morning, Stop & Shop, Malden Centre, two orders'. Uniqueness: he holds no other batch.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_event_id: Value d3858c0a-1ae0-4ccd-8865-8493a3e23288.
